gap: No result ChatGPT got states that "8K" is a USB bus-speed property (a full-speed USB device is polled at most once per 1 ms frame, a high-speed one once per 125 µs microframe, eight per millisecond), so the 0.125 ms that makers print is the report interval and not key-to-PC latency, and the figure only carries to the 2.4 GHz dongle where the maker says so.
standout_why: Compared against keebspicks.net (cited), Notebookcheck's HE75 Mag review (cited), hlplanet.com's Hall effect guide, setupinsider.com's two pages and dejaflow.com; Tom's Guide and both PC Gamer pages returned only navigation, so their bodies were not compared. Rivals have part of it: keebspicks gives a wired-versus-2.4 GHz split for the AULA F75 HE (8,000 Hz wired, 1,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz) and says latency claims come from brands; Notebookcheck notes "1,000 Hz max tested via wireless" on the HE75 Mag; hlplanet's guide says a dongle typically adds 20-100% latency. None gives the USB frame/microframe reason, none ties 0.125 ms to one microframe, and none sets a maker's own wired and wireless figures beside a measured pair for the under-$100 75% boards. hlplanet's guide lists the Yunzii RT75 Pro as "1000Hz polling, wired only", which contradicts Yunzii's own page. Not a 3, because the per-mode split is partly on a cited page and I could not open the AULA, MCHOSE or Gamakay product pages to complete the per-mode table.
decides: It splits the question by how the board will be connected. On a cable, every candidate I read claims 8,000 Hz, so price and switch decide, and HLPlanet's measurements of two 8K boards (0.60 and 0.65 ms wired) show the 0.125 ms claim is not the latency. On the 2.4 GHz dongle, only boards whose 8K is stated or listed for 2.4 GHz qualify. Yunzii states it for the RT75 Pro ($79.99), with its own 0.1 ms wired / 1 ms wireless figures; HLPlanet lists it for our Gamakay TK75 TMR ($89.99) and measured 0.75 ms on 2.4 GHz against 1.01 ms for the RT75 Pro with the same tool. So the TK75 TMR honestly wins the "fastest measured on the dongle under $100" segment. Gamakay's own NS75 guide claims 8,000 Hz only for wired, so the NS75 ($63.99) should be presented as an 8K-on-cable board with wireless as a convenience. The Epomaker HE80 ($59.49) is described by Epomaker as wired.

findings.label: USB polling period by bus speed (why 8,000 Hz needs a high-speed USB link)
findings.value: Full speed: period counted in 1 ms frames, minimum 1 frame (1,000 Hz). High speed: period counted in microframes, 8 per 1 ms frame, minimum 1 microframe (125 µs, 8,000 Hz).
findings.note: Microsoft's words: "For devices and host controllers that can operate at high speed, the period is measured in units of microframes. There are eight microframes in each 1 millisecond frame." bInterval "reflects the device's configuration in firmware. Drivers cannot change it." Arithmetic: 1 ms / 8 = 0.125 ms, so 1 / 0.125 ms = 8,000 reports per second. The page describes the USB specification's endpoint descriptor (section 9.6.6); it does not mention keyboards.
